subject: RetailCo - timeouts & 5xx surge after model v2.1 quantization rollout
messages:
From: Sara Lawson <sara.lawson@retailco.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
Cc: infra@retailco.com
Date: 2027-02-14T09:12:23-08:00
Subject: Sudden increase in 5xx/429 & client timeouts since 02:00 PST

Diego —

We pushed the model v2.1 default yesterday night (quantized profile Q3) and since ~02:00 PST this morning our app is seeing a sharp spike in 5xx/429 and a lot of client-side timeouts. Attached is a short CSV summarizing error counts by route and hour.

Key symptoms:
- Elevated 5xx and 429 across short text generation routes (prompt length <= 128).
- Some requests are hanging for ~10s before timing out.
- Retry storms on our side (clients retrying aggressively) leading to cascading load.

This is impacting checkout personalization for a small percentage of sessions but it’s enough to be visible in our funnel; we’re seeing ~2% drop in conversions on affected cohorts. Can you confirm if you see a correlating event on your side and what the immediate mitigation plan is?

We need either a quick rollback or a mitigation we can enable from our side.

— Sara
Head of Integrations, RetailCo

Attachments: retailco_error_summary.csv (text/csv, 22KB)

From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lawson <sara.lawson@retailco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-14T09:18:51-08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden increase in 5xx/429 & client timeouts since 02:00 PST

Sara — thanks for the quick heads up and the attachment. We’re looking into it now.

Immediate notes:
- I’ve opened an internal incident (INC-20270214-87) and looped in SRE + model infra.
- Can you confirm whether you pinned any shards to the new quantized variant or if you were relying on the default rollout? Any per-route overrides?
- We may need logs from client traces (trace IDs) for 09:30–10:00 PST if possible.

I’ve asked Marissa and Hannah to triage kernel/quantization regressions and verify whether a hotfix rollback to v2.0 is required. Expect an update in 20–30m.

— Diego
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachment: n/a

From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-14T09:28:07-08:00
Subject: RetailCo incident — initial triage request (INC-20270214-87)

Team —

RetailCo reports a surge of 5xx/429 and client timeouts coincident with our rollout of model v2.1 (quant profile Q3). They are high priority (checkout impact). Initial asks:
1) Check model runtime logs for kernel selection failures & OOMs across all hosts serving v2.1 during 02:00–03:30 PST.
2) Verify if quantized kernels fell back to slower code paths or raised errors for short sequences (<=128).
3) Produce a short latency distribution & 5xx/429 rate chart by host.
4) If we have a quick rollback play (v2.0), prepare the runbook and a plan for a 10-min tested rollback during low traffic.

Attached: kernel_profile.pcap from a repro run (instrumented VM) — please analyze. I’ll CTRL+F the logs and surface anything that looks like repeated retry loops from our side.

Note: keep RetailCo CC’d only for customer-facing comms. I’m looping Evelyn since this may need exec approval for credits if rollback impacts SLAs.

— Diego

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-14T10:04:39-08:00
Subject: Re: RetailCo incident — initial triage request (INC-20270214-87)

Quick update from runtime analysis (10:00):
- We see a pattern where the quantized kernel selector (Q3) chooses a low-memory kernel for sequence lengths under 128. On a subset of GPU hosts, this kernel is hitting an unexpected memory fragmentation path and triggering transient alloc failures. Those failures manifest as 5xx errors and in some cases long tail latency as the runtime retries an alternative path.
- Host-level metrics show repeated short-lived spikes in kernel load, which coincides with the client's retry behavior and amplifies the load (classic retry storm).
- No obvious network partition. This looks like a model-serving regression tied to the quantization profile + kernel selection heuristics.

Mitigation options (ranked):
A) Immediate customer-side mitigation: increase client-side retry backoff and reduce aggressive retries (we sent suggested headers). But RetailCo has limited ability to change client code quickly during peak traffic.
B) Platform-side hotfix: disable Q3 quantized kernel selector for the affected host group (safe mode) and switch to v2.1 unquantized kernel. This requires a config flip — low risk and measurable.
C) Full rollback: revert traffic for RetailCo to v2.0 (non-quantized) — higher blast radius but fastest confidence.

I’ve attached a dashboard screenshot showing 5xx rate by host and the sample kernel trace. Recommend B for an immediate 30–60min mitigation while we validate A/B. If no improvement, escalate to C.

Attachments: dashboard-screenshot-5xx.png, kernel_sample_trace.txt

From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lawson <sara.lawson@retailco.com>, Tom Beckett <t.beckett@retailco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-14T10:27:12-08:00
Subject: Action: temporary disable Q3 kernel selector + planned rollback window (ETA 10:45 PST)

Sara / Tom —

Thanks for the sample data. Based on our triage, this appears tied to the Q3 quantized kernel selector for v2.1. We’re going to perform a two-step mitigation:

1) Immediate (10:35 PST): flip platform config to disable Q3 kernel selection for hosts serving RetailCo traffic and route them to the unquantized/v2.1 path. Expected impact: reduce 5xx and remove the kernel alloc failures.
2) Contingency (11:00–11:10 PST): if step 1 does not materially improve errors, we will rollback RetailCo to model v2.0. We will not change global routing; this is a targeted rollback for RetailCo’s traffic.

We’ll monitor for 30 minutes after the config flip and share live dashboard links. If you prefer an immediate rollback instead of the Q3 flip, let me know and we can do C now.

We’ve scheduled a short call at 10:40 PST to confirm — invite to follow.

— Diego

Attachment: rollback-runbook.md

From: Sara Lawson <sara.lawson@retailco.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
Cc: infra@retailco.com, Tom Beckett <t.beckett@retailco.com>
Date: 2027-02-14T13:48:05-08:00
Subject: Re: Action: temporary disable Q3 kernel selector + planned rollback window (ETA 10:45 PST)

Diego —

Thanks — we saw immediate improvement after the config flip. 5xx dropped to baseline within ~8 minutes and client timeouts normalized. Appreciate quick handling.

Next steps per our side:
- We’ll keep conservative retry backoff for 48h.
- Please share the postmortem when available and the plan for a permanent fix (kernel selector heuristic or different quant profile).
- We’ll want a small credit against Feb usage for the SLA impact; happy to coordinate with your account team.

Please keep Evelyn and the incident channel updated; we’ll standby for the postmortem.

— Sara

Signature: Sara Lawson, Head of Integrations, RetailCo
